issues.title: Messaging migration footgun: 999/1000/1001 apply order silently weakens RLS
issues.description: backend/999-messaging-final-fix.sql and backend/999-messaging-production-fix.sql are byte-identical; neither has the v_is_participant hardening that 1000-phase6-messaging-reply-fix.sql / 1001-*.sql have. Filenames sort as strings, so applying the folder alphabetically installs the hardened version then silently overwrites it with the weaker one. backend/README.md only documents the 999-production-fix.sql path.
issues.impact: A routine 'run every .sql in order' deploy can silently downgrade messaging RLS after it was already hardened, with no error or warning. Unresolved across 4+ audit rounds because prior one-off SQL edits didn't survive re-delivery.
issues.solution: Needs a structural safeguard (e.g. a duplicate-function-definition check added to check:architecture), not another one-off SQL patch. Consider renaming files so lexical sort matches intended apply order, or adding a migration-order manifest the deploy script reads instead of globbing.

issues.title: public.users missing-row RLS bug — fix delivered but never confirmed applied
issues.description: Users missing a row in public.users hit an RLS failure. fix-users-rls.sql and backfill-missing-user.sql were written and handed off (including a backfill for account id 4979de85-3b3e-4826-aba6-200fcde9c7c4 on project hbvqvqlhvmeegtrmqvyo) but application was never confirmed against the live database.
issues.impact: Affected users likely still can't read/write their own profile row until this is actually run against the live project.
issues.solution: Confirm fix-users-rls.sql and backfill-missing-user.sql have actually been run against hbvqvqlhvmeegtrmqvyo, not just delivered.

issues.title: property_images 403 on insert — root cause never isolated
issues.description: Inserting a property image returns 403. Diagnosed as either a missing migration or an owner/session mismatch, but which of the two was never actually confirmed.
issues.impact: Landlords intermittently can't upload property photos, with no clear reproduction path yet.
issues.solution: Isolate which of the two hypotheses is correct with a direct reproduction against the live project before attempting a fix.

issues.title: ESLint is configured but cannot actually run
issues.description: eslint.config.js imports @eslint/js, which is missing from devDependencies. There's no lint npm script either. Running it cold fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Unchanged across every audit so far.
issues.impact: Would plausibly have caught real past bugs in this project — including a missing-import ReferenceError that shipped in PropertyDetail.jsx (phase6) and was only caught by an actual component mount, not a build.
issues.solution: Add @eslint/js to devDependencies, add a lint script to package.json, run it once cold to surface the current violation count.

issues.title: Main bundle not code-split — ~876.6KB / 239.5KB gzip
issues.description: Vite's own build warning, unaddressed across every audit. core/infrastructure/indexeddb.js is both statically and dynamically imported in different places, which defeats that module's chunk-splitting on its own.
issues.impact: Slower initial load, especially on mobile/lower-bandwidth connections — this is a Capacitor-wrapped app targeting mobile users.
issues.solution: Pick one import style for indexeddb.js (static or dynamic, not both) as the first step, then re-check the Vite build warning.

issues.title: HomeFilterBar.jsx is the largest remaining unsplit file (558 lines)
issues.description: Most other historically-large files in this project have already been split one at a time (PropertyDetail, PostCard, StudentPage, ContractorsPage, ContractorProfileView, SearchPage, MessageThreadView — see the completed items below). This is the next one in line.
issues.impact: Harder to review, test, and reason about than the already-split files.
issues.solution: Apply the same incremental split-and-verify process used on the prior seven files: real build + vitest + a jsdom mount exercising multiple render states, not just a syntax check.

issues.title: MessageTicks.jsx has a byte-identical, unreferenced dead duplicate
issues.description: src/pages/MessagesPage/MessageTicks.jsx is a byte-identical, unreferenced duplicate of src/features/messaging/components/MessageThread/MessageTicks.jsx. The phase13 messaging rebuild recreated it from scratch instead of moving the original.
issues.impact: Dead code adds confusion for the next person editing message-tick rendering — easy to edit the wrong copy.
issues.solution: Delete the unreferenced copy under pages/MessagesPage; worth a repo-wide dead-file sweep next time messaging is touched.

issues.title: src/features/* layer is real and wired in but undocumented by phase13's own report
issues.description: A substantial parallel src/features/* layer (features/messaging, features/properties, features/landlord, features/account) exists and is genuinely wired in — confirmed via grep, not dead code — but phase13's own architecture report doesn't mention it. The canonical documented data layer is src/core/ + src/core/data/domains + src/core/data/adapters.
issues.impact: Anyone reading only the phase report gets an incomplete picture of the real architecture, which undersells actual reality rather than overselling it.
issues.solution: Update the architecture docs to cover both src/core/ and src/features/*, and how they relate.

issues.title: No in-app way to grant admin/staff roles — Supabase Dashboard only
issues.description: Role model only recognizes admin/super_admin/moderator/staff. There is no in-app UI to grant app_metadata.role to a user — it must be set directly in the Supabase Dashboard.
issues.impact: Operationally awkward for onboarding new staff/moderators, and puts a manual, unaudited step between 'decide someone is staff' and 'they actually have staff access.'
issues.solution: A super-admin-only in-app role management screen, backed by a SECURITY DEFINER RPC with its own audit log.

issues.title: Migrations 031-052 and 999-1001 never confirmed applied against the live project
issues.description: Migrations 013-030 are confirmed run successfully against the live project by the user. Everything from 031-052 plus 999-1001 has unconfirmed live status. backend/README.md's own numbered run order stops documenting at 037.
issues.impact: Unclear whether the schema the app code assumes actually matches the live database beyond migration 030.
issues.solution: Run a live schema diff against the full migration set and update backend/README.md to document the full run order, not just up to 037.

issues.title: 6 of 17 test files are Docker/Postgres-skipped stubs asserting nothing at the RLS/RPC layer
issues.description: Test suite passes 65/65 across 17 files as of phase13, including 2 new real contract tests added in phase13 (architecture-boundaries.test.js, error-contract.test.js). But 6 of the 17 files are Docker/Postgres-skipped stubs that assert nothing about actual RLS or RPC behavior — the green checkmark overstates real coverage.
issues.impact: A fully green test run doesn't mean RLS/RPC behavior is actually verified — this has to be re-checked each audit rather than trusted from the pass count alone.
issues.solution: Either get the Docker/Postgres environment running in CI so those 6 files actually execute, or replace them with tests that don't require it.

issues.title: SearchPage's mobile detail sheet is unreachable on real mobile devices
issues.description: Found during the phase11 SearchPage split (771→130 lines) — not a regression from the split itself, a pre-existing bug. The 'mobile detail sheet' UI path is unreachable on actual mobile devices.
issues.impact: Mobile users likely can't access a piece of the search detail UI at all.
issues.solution: Reproduce on a real device (not just a resized desktop browser) to find the actual trigger condition, then fix.

issues.title: MessageList/MessageComposer re-render the whole Messages page on any controller state change
issues.description: MessageList and MessageComposer aren't wrapped in React.memo, and their callback props (retryMessage, formatMessageTime, handleViewingResponse) aren't useCallback-stabilized in useMessagesPageController.js. Any state change anywhere in that shared controller — a keystroke in the composer's inputValue, which lives in the same controller — re-renders the whole Messages page. Flagged as a bigger follow-up, not yet attempted.
issues.impact: Likely the next visible performance complaint on the Messages page; needs memo + stable callbacks together to actually help, not one alone.
issues.solution: Wrap MessageList/MessageComposer in React.memo and stabilize the controller's callback props with useCallback, verified together (partial fixes here have not helped in the past — see phase16 below).

issues.title: Global presence channel broadcast was O(n²) — every heartbeat notified every other online user
issues.description: Every 20s heartbeat also called channel.track() on one shared global Realtime presence channel, broadcasting to every other online user — C concurrent users meant C×(C−1) message deliveries per tick, not C. At ~20-40 concurrent users on the Messages page this could burn a large fraction of Supabase's monthly realtime-message quota from presence alone.
issues.impact: Would have hit Supabase's realtime quota (free: 2M msgs/mo, Pro $25/mo: 5M) from presence heartbeats alone well before real usage volume.
issues.solution: Removed the shared channel/track() broadcast entirely; useGlobalPresence now only runs the heartbeat_presence() RPC write. useChatPresence already had its own correctly-scoped per-user postgres_changes subscription. Disclosed trade-off: lost the instant 'went offline on tab close' signal — a departed user now reads offline once last_seen_at goes stale instead of immediately.

issues.title: Landlord got zero confirmation when declining a viewing request or a tenant cancelling one
issues.description: The 'ImbaLink assistant' bubble explaining a declined/cancelled viewing request was gated !isPropertyOwner, so the landlord side never saw it. Worse than it sounds: backend/047-viewing-request-assistant-messages.sql had already removed the plain-text fallback for these two statuses, relying solely on this client-side bubble.
issues.impact: Landlords declining or having a viewing request cancelled on them got no in-app confirmation at all that anything happened.
issues.solution: Dropped the owner gate; bubble now shows to both sides with role-appropriate copy, derived purely from msg.viewingRequestStatus. Verified via a direct MessageList mount across 6 cases (declined/cancelled × landlord/tenant, plus accepted/requested as negative controls).

issues.title: Messages hidden behind the composer on send and receive — scroll-margin guessing broke under late image loads
issues.description: First pass (phase16) scrolled a sentinel div via scrollIntoView + a guessed margin, and only one of two auto-scroll effects set scrollMarginBottom at all. Real root cause found in phase17: the scroll could land short if a message's attachment image was still loading when the scroll fired, since the container grows after the scroll already happened — affecting both send and receive equally.
issues.impact: Newest messages were sometimes visually hidden behind the composer, on both sending and receiving a message.
issues.solution: Added a scrollContainerRef threaded through useMessagesPageController → MessagesPage.jsx → MessageThreadView.jsx, attached to the actual scrollable div, and rewrote useMessageViewport.js to set container.scrollTop = container.scrollHeight directly, re-checked across two requestAnimationFrames to catch a late image-driven layout shift. Verified with a mount test simulating a late scrollHeight growth mid-flight.

issues.title: PropertyDetail.jsx shipped a top-level ReferenceError on every mount from a missing import
issues.description: Found while splitting PropertyDetail.jsx (1040→337 lines). PHASE-N-REPORT.md files in this project have a documented history of claiming 'syntax scan: 0 errors' / 'architecture checker passed' without a real build/render ever being performed — this bug is the concrete example: neither a syntax scan nor a plain vite build catches a missing-import ReferenceError, only an actual component mount does.
issues.impact: Every mount of PropertyDetail.jsx threw, undetected by the checks the project's own reports claimed had passed.
issues.solution: Fixed the missing import. This is also why the file-splitting process since phase6 has required a real jsdom/react-dom mount exercising multiple render states for every split, not just a build or syntax check.

issues.title: PropertyDetail, PostCard, StudentPage, ContractorsPage, ContractorProfileView, SearchPage, MessageThreadView — all split from 700-1000+ line files
issues.description: PropertyDetail.jsx (1040→337, phase6), PostCard.jsx (905→200, phase7), StudentPage.jsx (744→94, phase8), ContractorsPage.jsx (831→110, phase9), ContractorProfileView.jsx (766→73, phase10), SearchPage.jsx (771→130, phase11), MessageThreadView.jsx (647→92, phase12, deliberately a conservative 2-file split since most of its bulk was one repeated per-message render block). All delivered as separate incremental zips, each verified with check:architecture + npm run build + vitest run + a real jsdom/react-dom mount exercising multiple render states.
issues.impact: Seven of the project's largest, hardest-to-review files are now properly decomposed. HomeFilterBar.jsx (558 lines) is next in line — see MAINT-001.
issues.solution: Completed across phases 6-12. Recurring lesson: token colors and verbatim text moved into new small files are an easy silent-drift spot — diff-check extractions rather than eyeballing them.

issues.title: Dead BottomNav.jsx and mockMessagingProvider.js removed
issues.description: Both files were previously flagged as dead code, and were falsely claimed fixed in docs for several rounds before actually being removed. Confirmed gone as of phase13.
issues.impact: Reduces dead-code confusion; also a reminder that a doc claiming something is fixed isn't the same as it being fixed — this took several rounds to actually verify.
issues.solution: Removed.

issues.title: Two different migration files are both numbered 041
issues.description: 041-public-landlord-listings-gallery.sql and 041-support-requests.sql share the same migration number. Both are real, distinct migrations (public landlord gallery visibility vs. support request records) — this is not a duplicate/dead file, just a numbering collision.
issues.impact: Anyone applying migrations by sorted filename could run these in either order depending on secondary sort (a/p vs a/s), and any future numbered-migration tooling that assumes uniqueness would break on this pair.
issues.solution: Renumber one of the two (e.g. to 043, since 043 does not exist) and update backend/README.md accordingly.
